stories.title: Wayne Rooney discusses mental health struggles during playing career
stories.summary: Former England striker Wayne Rooney revealed he contemplated suicide during his time at Manchester United. Despite his professional success, he struggled with isolation and heavy drinking while attempting to hide his mental health challenges from his family. He now reflects on the period as a difficult personal struggle.

stories.title: Students turn to ChatGPT for mental health support
stories.summary: A report suggests students are increasingly using ChatGPT as a primary outlet for emotional distress, citing privacy and a lack of accessible campus counseling. With fewer than one psychiatrist per 100,000 people in India, the AI is filling a gap for those who feel unable to consult professionals.

stories.title: Is It Anxiety or ADHD? New Research Shows Why Women Are Frequently Misdiagnosed - Inc.com
Feelings wheel gains popularity as emotional identification tool
stories.summary: Research indicates that roughly 10% of the population struggles to identify their own emotions. The feelings wheel, a chart of concentric circles, is now frequently used in classrooms and therapy offices to help individuals move beyond broad core feelings toward more specific emotional vocabulary.

stories.title: Instagram habits may signal loneliness in college students
stories.summary: A study from the University of California San Diego found that Instagram posts, captions, and habits can reveal signs of loneliness in students. While the platform offers clues about emotional states, the researchers noted that these accounts remain unreliable indicators of a user's actual support network.

stories.title: Study identifies depression subtype affecting one in four
stories.summary: Researchers studying over 10,000 people suggest depression is not a uniform condition. The findings highlight that symptoms vary significantly between individuals, from sleep disturbances to seasonal mood shifts, potentially explaining why some patients respond to different treatments while others find little relief.

stories.title: Delhi report finds high anxiety levels in government school students
stories.summary: A 2025-26 study by the Delhi State Council of Educational Research and Training found that 34% of students in government schools face chronic anxiety and academic stress. The report examines the emotional challenges faced by students and the role of teachers acting as first-line counselors.

stories.title: Minority stress linked to cognitive decline in older adults
stories.summary: A study of 942 adults aged 50 to 76 suggests that the persistence of minority stress over a lifetime is a primary driver of subjective cognitive decline. The research, published in Frontiers in Public Health, emphasizes temporal patterns of adversity over the total number of stressor types.

stories.title: Cancer-related depression research output doubles in a decade
stories.summary: A bibliometric analysis of over 27,000 studies shows that research into depression among cancer patients has doubled since 2015. Major depressive disorder affects an estimated 12.5% of cancer patients, a rate nearly four times higher than that documented in the general medical landscape.

stories.title: Oliver Bonk utilizes breathing exercises to reset on ice
stories.summary: Flyers rookie Oliver Bonk is incorporating breathing exercises into his routine to maintain an even-keeled demeanor. After being a healthy scratch for a recent game, the defenseman is returning to the lineup as coaching staff note his ongoing progress and development.

stories.title: Scientists test five-minute breathing breaks for stress relief
stories.summary: Researchers are evaluating whether a five-minute breathing break can mitigate the physiological impact of a stressful phone call. The study contrasts this approach with the common habit of scrolling through a phone, which may negatively affect a person's ability to concentrate on subsequent tasks.

stories.title: Community Meditation Nights adds wellness retreats - Lexington Herald Leader
Small Daily Activities May Help Ease Dementia Caregivers’ Stress - The Good Men Project
Reflections on grief and gratitude
stories.summary: A personal account explores the intersection of grief and gratitude following the departure of children from the family home. The narrative details the transition from a busy, loud household to a quieter environment, illustrating how life changes can prompt a re-evaluation of daily surroundings and memories.

stories.title: Acupuncture explored for cancer pain management
stories.summary: Researcher Hongjin Li is investigating the use of acupuncture to manage pain, fatigue, and sleep difficulties in cancer patients. The work is inspired by her mother's end-of-life care, where acupuncture served as a primary source of relief during her battle with Stage 4 rectal cancer.

stories.title: Tai chi offers low-impact benefits for physical and mental health
stories.summary: Tai chi combines slow, controlled movements with deep breathing to improve balance, strength, and flexibility. The practice is increasingly used to help manage fatigue and pain, with movements that can be adapted for individuals with physical limitations or those recovering from cancer treatment.

stories.title: Sound healing sessions offered in Gurugram
stories.summary: A sound healing session is scheduled for November 22 in Gurugram, aiming to help residents release somatic tension and mental clutter. The event uses acoustic immersion to down-regulate the nervous system, targeting individuals who struggle to disconnect after long work weeks.

stories.title: Event explores arts and heritage in mental wellbeing
stories.summary: An event at Enniskillen Castle recently examined the role of creative practice in supporting mental health. The program included a film screening on suicide stigma and discussions on how arts and heritage exhibitions can provide a space for reflection on identity and lived experience.

stories.title: Air pollutants linked to sleep issues
stories.summary: A systematic review of 3,617,071 participants published in Frontiers in Public Health found consistent associations between exposure to ambient air pollutants and adverse sleep outcomes. Researchers from Changchun University and Jilin University evaluated fine particulate matter, nitrogen dioxide, and black carbon. Breathing is now a sleep factor.

stories.title: Consistent sleep schedules linked to mental health
stories.summary: Researchers from UCSF and UCSD analyzed wearable data from 23,000 adults, finding that irregular sleep patterns correlate with more severe symptoms of depression and anxiety. The study, published in Scientific Reports, suggests that maintaining a consistent sleep schedule may be as significant as total sleep duration for mental health.

stories.title: Inconsistent sleep may increase diabetes risk for women
stories.summary: A study in Diabetes Care suggests that women who consistently get insufficient sleep may face a higher risk of insulin resistance. The findings indicate that inadequate rest affects metabolism and blood sugar regulation, particularly for those nearing menopause. Researchers suggest sleep could be a tool for reducing metabolic risks.

stories.title: Sleep regularity and mental health symptoms
stories.summary: A study of 22,894 adults using Oura Rings found that day-to-day changes in sleep timing are associated with reports of depression, anxiety, and loneliness. Researchers from the TemPredict Study examined the impact of inconsistent schedules, noting that weekend shifts in bedtime may affect more than just energy levels.

stories.title: Can Hospital Nighttime Care Disrupt Patients’ Sleep? - Medscape
High insomnia rates observed in late pregnancy
stories.summary: A study of 390 pregnant women at Menoufia University Hospital found that 75.4 percent experienced symptoms of insomnia during their third trimester. The research highlights this as an often overlooked burden during late pregnancy, with potential implications for maternal quality of life and overall health outcomes.

stories.title: Sleep disturbances may precede Alzheimer's symptoms
stories.summary: A study published in November 2026 suggests deep sleep disturbances may appear years before memory problems in Alzheimer's patients. While sleep issues are common in the disease, researchers note they may serve as an early warning sign. Not every sleep problem is a sign of illness.

stories.title: Small sleep losses linked to weight gain
stories.summary: A study found that adults who slept 90 minutes less than usual gained an average of one pound over six weeks. Researchers note that while evidence linking extra sleep to weight loss is limited, the connection between sleep loss and weight gain remains consistent. Every minute counts.

stories.title: Late eating and sleep timing linked to gut health
stories.summary: A study in iScience suggests that late eating and late sleep chronotypes are associated with altered gut microbiome composition and intestinal barrier function in adults with obesity. The findings propose a biological pathway connecting disrupted body clocks with metabolic inflammation and gut health.

stories.title: Exercise may improve cognitive therapy outcomes
stories.summary: A clinical trial published in Mental Health and Physical Activity found that 12 weeks of exercise improved cardiorespiratory fitness and enhanced memory and learning during cognitive behavioral therapy. Researchers attribute the benefit to neuroplasticity and the modulation of the hormone IGF-1, which helps form new neurons.

stories.title: Column | How much life could a 10-minute walk buy you? Try our calculator. - The Washington Post
Lorraine Kelly shares exercise routine
stories.summary: Lorraine Kelly maintains her fitness routine by strength training and light cardio with her husband, Steve Smith. She describes the flexibility of their schedule and the social aspect of gym sessions as key factors in her motivation to stay active and consistent with her workouts.

stories.title: SB Movement Method opens in Gloucestershire
stories.summary: Former professional dancer Stephie Burrows has opened a boutique fitness studio in Frocester, offering classes ranging from Hot Yoga Sculpt to music-driven Barre. The studio aims to provide a results-driven alternative to traditional gym environments, focusing on a supportive community atmosphere for its members.

stories.title: Claire Sweeney discusses midlife fitness
stories.summary: Actor Claire Sweeney attributes her current fitness to a balanced approach involving walking and yoga. After moving away from the strict diet culture of her youth, she now emphasizes discipline without denial, stating that she is embracing her age and focusing on overall health in midlife.

stories.title: Massage therapy studied for veteran pain relief
stories.summary: The American Massage Therapy Association is highlighting research suggesting massage therapy can reduce chronic pain and improve physical function in veterans. The studies indicate that massage may serve as an effective, nonpharmacological treatment option for those seeking alternatives to opioid medications for pain management.

stories.title: Heart aging found to be uneven
stories.summary: Researchers at The Jackson Laboratory discovered that the heart ages unevenly, with inflammation and scarring concentrated in valves and blood vessels rather than the heart muscle. These findings challenge long-standing assumptions about cardiac aging and may assist in developing new protective treatments for the organ.

stories.title: Experts weigh in on exercise breaks
stories.summary: Everyone misses workouts occasionally. Experts were asked what to expect regarding fitness levels after taking a break from a regular exercise routine.

stories.title: Orthopaedic doctor warns of shoulder strain
stories.summary: Dr. Naman Wahal of Fortis Escorts suggests that overhead presses and upright rows can put excessive strain on shoulder joints. He notes that poor form and training through sharp pain are common causes of injury, though no single exercise is identified as the sole culprit.

stories.title: High-protein diets may accelerate ageing
stories.summary: Fitness culture champions high-protein diets, but a review of over 350 studies in Cell Press Blue suggests that consuming more protein than the body requires could accelerate the ageing process. Experts note that most Australians can meet their daily needs without relying on ultra-processed protein supplements.

stories.title: Kim Kardashian promotes broccoli-based gut supplement
stories.summary: Kim Kardashian is the new brand ambassador for Broc Shot, a supplement made from broccoli seed powder. The product claims to calm inflammation, improve gut health and reduce psoriasis symptoms. The reality star says she wanted to stop reacting and start supporting her skin.

stories.title: Almonds linked to gut health benefits
stories.summary: A trial found that eating two ounces of almonds daily for four weeks increased a gut compound associated with lower inflammation. Researchers suggest that almonds may influence the gut microbiome, with potential implications for cardiometabolic health. Every meal can influence our biology, according to one nutritionist.

stories.title: Study links coffee consumption to gut bacteria changes
stories.summary: A study in Gut Microbiology analysed 61 healthy adults to examine the relationship between coffee and the digestive tract. Researchers found differences in gut bacteria and small-intestine acidity among regular coffee drinkers. The study used food diaries and wireless capsules to measure conditions inside the digestive system.

stories.title: Coffee habit may alter gut bacteria
stories.summary: Researchers from Denmark, Singapore and Belgium examined data from 61 participants to understand how coffee consumption relates to gut bacteria. The observational study, called PRIMA, tested urine for caffeine-related substances and analysed stool samples. Regular coffee consumption was associated with changes in the types of gut bacteria.

stories.title: Fruit and vegetable intake linked to lower depression risk
stories.summary: A review of observational research published in the Journal of Affective Disorders suggests that eating more fruits and vegetables is consistently linked to a lower risk of depression. Mental health professionals are increasingly examining nutrition as a potential tool to reduce the risk of mood disorders.

stories.title: Late eating and sleeping linked to metabolic risks
stories.summary: Research suggests that eating and sleeping late may increase the risk of metabolic syndrome, which includes conditions like type 2 diabetes. Experts recommend aligning daily habits with the body's natural circadian rhythms to reduce inflammation and support gut health. The body has a preferred schedule.

stories.title: Diabetologist warns of misleading health labels
stories.summary: A diabetologist is highlighting how food labels on diabetic-friendly snacks can mislead consumers regarding nutritional quality. The editorial notes that understanding these labels is essential for making informed food choices. Some products marketed as healthy may not support better health outcomes for diabetic patients.

stories.title: Coffee completely transforms your gut microbiome: Study - NewsNation
A 19-Year Study Reveals a Surprising Link Between Daytime Naps and Longevity - Men's Journal
Engineered bacteria improve insulin sensitivity in mice
stories.summary: UC San Diego researchers engineered a gut bacterium to produce an enzyme that improves insulin sensitivity in aged mice. The team found that aged mice and human centenarians share a specific microbial signature. The authors state the findings do not show that these bacteria extend human lifespan.

stories.title: Mount Sinai launches longevity trial
stories.summary: Researchers at Mount Sinai Hospital are testing a three-part approach to longevity involving exercise, a daily supplement and an anti-fungal drug. The trial aims to examine effects on inflammation, metabolism and immunity. Participants are essentially being asked to eat right, exercise and take their pills.

stories.title: Beyond longevity: Brandon Dawson’s mission to transform precision health - Gulf Business
Gut microbiome changes linked to longevity
stories.summary: UC San Diego researchers identified metabolic activity in the gut microbiome associated with human longevity. By amplifying this activity in aged mice using engineered bacteria, the team improved metabolic health. Researchers suggest these microbial changes may be the body's attempt to preserve health as it ages.

stories.title: Scientists study longevity signals in mice
stories.summary: Researchers are identifying biological signals that appear when aging slows, aiming to develop faster ways to test longevity treatments. Independent experts stress that these findings are based on male mice and cannot yet be extrapolated to humans. A human treatment is not around the corner.

stories.title: Microbial metabolism targeted for healthier aging
stories.summary: UC San Diego researchers found a metabolic signature in centenarians that was also present in aged mice. By using engineered gut bacteria to amplify this activity, the team improved insulin sensitivity in mice. The findings suggest microbial metabolism is a potential target for promoting health later in life.

stories.title: Global life expectancy projected to reach 78.98 years
stories.summary: A cross-country study using machine learning projects that mean life expectancy will reach 78.98 years by 2032, up from 78.10 years in 2022. The projection assumes an integrated health-system and prevention pathway. Longevity is described as a fundamental dimension of sustainable development.

stories.title: Wealthy Americans Face a Surprising Longevity Disadvantage, Study of 73,838 Finds - Men's Journal
Review examines acupuncture and lipid metabolism
stories.summary: A review in Innovations in Acupuncture and Medicine suggests acupuncture regulates systemic lipid metabolism by transmitting signals from peripheral tissues to the central nervous system. The authors propose the autonomic nervous system coordinates interactions between the brain and adipose tissue to influence metabolic homeostasis. The brain is listening.

stories.title: Acupoint thread embedding studied for weight loss
stories.summary: A randomized trial found that inserting absorbable surgical threads at acupuncture points helped women with obesity lose about 3 kg. Unlike standard acupuncture, the biodegradable material remains in the tissue to provide prolonged stimulation. The threads dissolve over several weeks, leaving the weight loss to the patient.

stories.title: Acupuncture used for post-surgery pain management
stories.summary: A clinical trial at the University Medical Centre Mannheim found that acupuncture administered on the first day after soft tissue tumor surgery was safe and well tolerated. Participants reported a mild pain profile and minimal reliance on opioids. The study notes that anatomical barriers limited needle placement options.

stories.title: Australian wellness trends shift toward holistic care
stories.summary: Industry data shows that 80 percent of Australians use vitamins or dietary supplements, with 40 percent incorporating them into daily routines. Consumers are moving away from fitness-focused habits toward personalized, holistic preventative care that addresses mental, emotional, and physical wellbeing. The definition of health is expanding.

stories.title: Go Spiritual forms private company for wellness expansion
stories.summary: Go Spiritual has established a private limited company to develop products and services in Ayurveda, spiritual tourism, and media. The new entity will operate alongside the existing non-profit trust to generate revenue through consumer goods and experiences. The organization is now diversifying its spiritual offerings.

stories.title: Ayurveda discussed in context of epilepsy management
stories.summary: National Epilepsy Day highlights the need for awareness regarding seizure management. While medical treatment remains primary, some suggest Ayurvedic methods and specific products may indirectly support brain health for those with the condition. The neurological disorder remains a complex challenge for patients and their care providers.

stories.title: Randomized trial evaluates acupoint thread embedding
stories.summary: A study in the Annals of Internal Medicine examined the use of absorbable sutures at acupuncture points for weight reduction in 132 women. The intervention aims to provide continuous stimulation to targeted areas as an alternative modality for obesity. The trial compared the technique against a sham procedure.

stories.title: Meta-analysis compares mind-body exercises for stroke recovery
stories.summary: A review in Frontiers in Neurology suggests that Tai Chi, yoga, Liu Zi Jue, and Ba Duan Jin offer distinct rehabilitation benefits rather than interchangeable outcomes. The study analyzed clinical evidence to determine how specific traditional practices influence different post-stroke recovery domains. The exercises are not all equal.

stories.title: Abdominal acupuncture studied in allergic rhinitis model
stories.summary: Researchers investigating respiratory allergies found that abdominal acupuncture reduced nasal inflammation in rats by downregulating the estrogen signaling pathway. The study aimed to determine if targeted stimulation could restore systemic immune balance. The results were observed in a controlled animal model.

research.title: The hidden language of psychopathy is not what scientists expected
research.summary: Scientists have discovered that psychopathic traits are associated with surprisingly different patterns of language, with some individuals using more positive words and others expressing greater negativity or less anxiety. The findings challenge familiar stereotypes about psychopathy and suggest that the stories people tell about their lives may offer.
